title: Multiply Using Recursion
statement:
Given two integers `a` and `b`, compute their product **without using the multiplication (`*`) or division (`/`) operators**. Addition, subtraction, comparison, negation and bit shifts are allowed. Either number may be negative or zero.

A recursive solution that adds `a` to itself `b` times works in O(|b|) time, but `b` can be as large as a billion, so it is too slow and recurses too deeply. Your solution needs to run in O(log(min(|a|, |b|))) time.

Print `a × b`.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer first asked for the simple recursive approach, then asked to improve it to O(log(min(a, b))). Think about how repeated halving of one factor and doubling of the other can replace repeated addition.
inputFormat: A single line containing the two integers `a` and `b`.
constraints: The product fits in a signed 64-bit integer

examples.explanation: The product of a negative and a positive number is negative: 5 × 12 = 60, so the result is -60.

hints: Handle the sign separately, then work with the absolute values. Adding `a` to itself `b` times is correct but far too slow.
Split on the parity of `b`: if `b` is even, `a × b = (2a) × (b / 2)`; if it is odd, `a × b = a + a × (b - 1)`.
Using the smaller number as the one you halve gives O(log(min(a, b))) steps. Note that the product can reach 10^18, which overflows doubles in JavaScript, so use BigInt.
